vulnerable_code:
from ninja import Router, File, UploadedFile
from ninja.security import HttpBearer
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404
from .models import CustomerKYCDocument
from .schemas import UploadStatusSchema

kyc_upload_router = Router(auth=HttpBearer())

@kyc_upload_router.post("/verifications/{verification_id}/id-document", response=UploadStatusSchema)
def upload_id_document(request, verification_id: int, document: UploadedFile = File(...)):
    # Resolves KYC verification record without verifying that caller owns it
    record = get_object_or_404(CustomerKYCDocument, id=verification_id)

    # Overwrites stored identity file with user-supplied upload
    record.document_file.save(document.name, document)
    record.save()

    return {"verification_id": record.id, "filename": document.name, "status": "uploaded"}
diagnosis: upload_id_document accepts an UploadedFile and attaches it to a CustomerKYCDocument resolved strictly by verification_id. Because the endpoint does not verify that the target verification record belongs to request.auth, an attacker can overwrite official government ID documents, passports, and driver's licenses of other banking customers with forged files during active KYC identity reviews.

corrected_code:
from ninja import Router, File, UploadedFile
from ninja.security import HttpBearer
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404
from .models import CustomerKYCDocument
from .schemas import UploadStatusSchema

kyc_upload_router = Router(auth=HttpBearer())

@kyc_upload_router.post("/verifications/{verification_id}/id-document", response=UploadStatusSchema)
def upload_id_document(request, verification_id: int, document: UploadedFile = File(...)):
    # Validate that the KYC verification record strictly belongs to the authenticated user
    record = get_object_or_404(
        CustomerKYCDocument,
        id=verification_id,
        user=request.auth
    )

    record.document_file.save(document.name, document)
    record.save()

    return {"verification_id": record.id, "filename": document.name, "status": "uploaded"}
